availability.workiva-ai: Included with Workiva AI once your organization has signed the Workiva AI Terms of Use. Your admin can limit it to some workspaces or users.
availability.entitlement: Depends on the Workiva solutions your organization has. Check with your Workiva team.
availability.unlisted: Workiva lists this ability, but no public support page we could read describes it yet. Check in your workspace whether it is on for you.
availability.preview: A preview Workiva offers to selected customers. Ask your Workiva team whether it is on for you.

chat.name: Workiva AI chat
chat.how: The sparkles icon at the top of the screen. One conversation follows you across documents, spreadsheets, presentations, Wdata and files.
steps: Open Workiva AI with the sparkles icon at the top of the screen.
Ask one specific question at a time, with the context it needs.
Check the Sources listed under the answer before you use it.

files.name: Workiva AI chat with workspace files
files.how: In chat, click Add workspace files or type @ (up to 10 files), or right-click a file and choose Ask Workiva AI. Files must be in your workspace first; chat takes no uploads. It reads text, numbers and charts, including scanned PDFs and images.
steps: Put the file in your workspace; Workiva AI chat cannot take uploads.
Open Workiva AI (the sparkles icon) and add the file with @ or Add workspace files, up to 10 files.
Paste the prompt below, then open the Sources it lists under the answer.

doc.name: Workiva AI in a document
doc.how: Open Workiva AI from the document, or select text and use a quick edit to shorten it, change the tone or elaborate. Insert the answer at your cursor, copy it, or Refine it.
steps: Open the document and select the section.
Choose the sparkles icon by your selection for a quick edit, or open Workiva AI and paste the prompt.
Insert or copy the result, then check every number against the source.

advisor.name: Prompt advisor
advisor.how: Ready-made prompts by industry. In Workiva AI chat, choose View prompt advisor, search or filter, then Use prompt.

sheet.name: Workiva AI in spreadsheets
sheet.how: Select cells, then choose Fix this formula, Explain this formula, Summarize data, Find trends, or ask about the selected cells. It returns formulas, not calculated values.

wdata.name: Workiva AI for Wdata queries
wdata.how: The sparkles icon in a query: describe what you need in plain language and it creates, improves, explains or fixes the SQL. No SQL knowledge required.

support-kb.name: Workiva Support Intelligence knowledge base
support-kb.how: In Workiva AI chat, click + Add Knowledge bases and choose Workiva Support Intelligence. Answers link to the Support Center articles and videos they used.
steps: Open Workiva AI chat with the sparkles icon.
Click + Add Knowledge bases and choose Workiva Support Intelligence.
Ask how to do the task, then follow the linked Support Center articles.

xbrl-help.name: AI Error Validation
xbrl-help.how: In the XBRL Validation Panel, select an error and choose Help me fix this. Workiva AI explains the error, the rule behind it and the steps to fix it. US-GAAP filings only.
steps: Generate XBRL for the filing to fill the Validation Panel.
Select a validation message and choose Help me fix this.
Apply the fix, regenerate XBRL and check that the error has cleared.

tie-out.name: Tie-out assistant (preview)
tie-out.how: Start a workflow in Workiva AI chat and choose Tie-out assistant, or open Tie-out Assistant from a document's Markup toolbar. It matches related figures across the document and lists possible differences for you to review. In preview, for 10-K and 10-Q documents.
steps: In Workiva AI chat choose Start a workflow, then Tie-out assistant.
Review each possible difference it lists; deciding what is wrong stays with you.

benchmarking.name: Benchmarking workflow (preview, Intelligent Finance)
benchmarking.how: Start a workflow in Workiva AI chat and choose Benchmarking. It compares the disclosures in your report with peer companies' and points out gaps and differences in language and structure.

sec-intel.name: SEC Filing Intelligence (Intelligent Finance)
sec-intel.how: From the Intelligent Finance icon, filter filings by keyword, peers, filing type and dates, and ask Workiva AI about the selected 10-K and 10-Q filings.

report-8k.name: Automated 8-K setup (preview)
report-8k.how: In Workiva AI choose Workflows, then Report generation (or Create, then Agentic report). Describe the event, confirm the SEC items and choose the source files; it drafts the 8-K for you to review.

grc-chat.name: Risk and Controls Intelligence (AI-Powered GRC)
grc-chat.how: A chat assistant inside GRC workflows, and a Risk & Control intelligence knowledge base you can add in Workiva AI chat.

control-creator.name: Control creator (AI-Powered GRC)
control-creator.how: Drafts a control from the definition of a risk.

test-steps.name: Test step and attribute generation (AI-Powered GRC)
test-steps.how: Generates test steps and attributes for a control.

flowchart.name: Flowchart visualizer (AI-Powered GRC)
flowchart.how: Builds a flowchart from process documentation, control and risk information.

risk-summary.name: Risk interview and risk activity summaries (AI-Powered GRC)
risk-summary.how: Summarizes risk interviews and risk activity.

esrs-issb.name: ESRS and ISSB intelligence (Intelligent sustainability)
esrs-issb.how: Add the ESRS, Revised ESRS or ISSB knowledge base in Workiva AI chat to summarize a standard and its disclosure requirements. Needs Sustainability Reporting Advanced; ESRS needs the CSRD add-on.

disclosure.name: Sustainability disclosure agent (Intelligent sustainability)
disclosure.how: Start a workflow in Workiva AI chat, or select text in a document and choose Quick edits, then Draft disclosure. It checks your draft against the ESRS or IFRS requirements you pick and returns a scorecard, action items and a draft narrative.

fitBasis.named: Workiva names a feature or example for this job.
fitBasis.assumed: No feature is named for this exact job; it is the general chat-with-files ability applied to it. Try it on one real file before relying on it.

evidence.heard: Customers described this task in their own words (explainer evidence audit; names removed).
evidence.pattern: A pattern across several customers in the explainer audit.
evidence.workiva: Workiva itself gives this as a use or example.

useCases.task: Write the first draft of the year-over-year change narrative.
useCases.prompt: Use only the current-year file and the prior-year file I selected with @. Context: this narrative goes to [who will read it] in the [section] of our report. Draft the year-over-year change narrative for [section], explaining each change of more than [threshold] in one or two sentences, as a short list. Use only figures in the files, keeping each amount and unit exactly as written with no currency added. Do not explain a change the files do not explain; mark it, and anything else I need to confirm, as [to confirm].
useCases.stays: Checking every figure, and deciding what is worth explaining.
useCases.try: Every quarter I draft the year-over-year change narrative for the MD&A.

useCases.task: Check that the figures agree throughout a 10-K or 10-Q draft.
useCases.stays: Investigating each difference, and the tie-out sign-off. In preview it covers 10-K and 10-Q documents only.
useCases.try: Every quarter I tie out the figures throughout the 10-Q draft.

useCases.task: Check that the narrative, the tables and related documents such as the earnings release say the same thing.
useCases.prompt: Use only the draft and the other document I selected with @. Context: the draft goes to review soon, so I need to catch mismatches first. Check them against each other and list every place where a number or statement does not match, as a table with the section and both values. Do not fix anything or guess; I will check each one.
useCases.stays: The tie-out itself and every correction. Keep to one section at a time for long filings.
useCases.try: Every close I tie out the numbers in the earnings release to the financial statements.

useCases.task: Explain the GAAP-to-statutory differences for each entity.
useCases.prompt: Use only the reconciliation file for [entity] I selected with @. Context: the explanations are for [who will read it], who is not an accountant. List each GAAP-to-statutory adjustment as a table with a one-line plain-English explanation of why it exists. Do not add facts that are not in the file; mark anything unclear as [to confirm].
useCases.stays: The math and the adjustments themselves. Excel files need your organization's AWS model provider turned on.
useCases.try: Every year I explain the GAAP-to-statutory differences for each entity.

useCases.task: See how our disclosures compare with peers' filings.
useCases.prompt: Use only the filing I selected with @ and the peer filings I name: [peer companies]. Context: I am preparing our [disclosure topic] disclosure for [who will read it]. Compare how they describe it with our wording, and list what they cover that we do not, as a table with where each appears. Do not add anything that is not in those filings.
useCases.stays: Deciding what, if anything, to change.
useCases.try: Each year I compare our risk factor disclosures with our peers' filings.

useCases.task: Understand and fix XBRL validation errors before filing.
useCases.stays: Applying each fix and the filing itself. The guidance is a starting point; compliance stays with your team. US-GAAP filings only.
useCases.try: Every quarter I fix the XBRL validation errors before we file.

useCases.task: Draft an 8-K after a material event.
useCases.stays: Every SEC item, figure and word. The draft is a starting point, not a final filing.
useCases.try: Each time we have a material event I draft the 8-K from the press release.

useCases.task: Pull the key points out of a long document before a meeting.
useCases.prompt: Use only the document I selected with @. Context: the summary is for [who will read it], who will not read the full file. Summarize it in five bullets, then list every point that needs a decision, with who decides and by when if the document says. Keep each amount and unit exactly as written with no currency added, and do not add facts that are not in the document; I will review it.
useCases.stays: What to act on. Check each Sources link Workiva AI lists under its answer.
useCases.try: Before each audit committee meeting I summarize the long memos into key points.

useCases.task: Answer questions about how to do something in Workiva.
useCases.prompt: Use only the Support Intelligence knowledge base. Context: I am helping a colleague who is new to [the task]. Explain how to [the task] in Workiva, as a numbered list of steps with a link to each Support Center article you used. If the articles do not cover it, say so rather than guess.
useCases.stays: Trying the steps in your own workspace; your setup and permissions may differ.
useCases.try: Every week I answer questions from colleagues about how to do things in Workiva.

useCases.task: Rewrite a section to be shorter or clearer for a different audience.
useCases.prompt: Use only the selected section. Context: it is going to [audience]. Rewrite it in under [number] words, as one short paragraph. Keep every number and fact exactly as written, and do not add anything new.
useCases.stays: The final wording, every number and fact, and the length: count the words yourself.
useCases.try: Every quarter I rewrite the CFO's commentary to be shorter for the board.

useCases.task: Explain or fix a formula in a spreadsheet.
useCases.stays: The numbers. Workiva AI returns formulas, not calculated values; check each one before you rely on it.
useCases.try: Every close I check the formulas in our spreadsheets and explain them to reviewers.

useCases.task: Write, explain or fix a Wdata query in plain language.
useCases.stays: Running the query and checking what it returns.
useCases.try: Every month I write SQL queries in Wdata to pull the data for each report.

useCases.task: Translate a document's content into another language.
useCases.stays: A native speaker's review before anything is published.
useCases.try: Every year I translate the annual report into French and German.

useCases.task: Find controls that overlap or duplicate each other.
useCases.prompt: You are an internal controls analyst. Use only the control list I selected with @. Context: we are looking for overlapping controls to simplify our testing. Group controls whose descriptions cover the same risk or activity, as a table with the control IDs and one line on why they look alike. Do not recommend removing any; I will decide.
useCases.stays: Which controls to merge or retire. Work through one process at a time for long lists.
useCases.try: We need to rationalize our controls, there are too many overlapping ones.

useCases.task: Map our existing controls to a new framework and see what is missing.
useCases.prompt: Use only the control list and the framework file I selected with @. Context: I am preparing a mapping to [framework] for [who will read it]. Map each control to the [framework] requirements as a table with a one-line reason for each match, mark weak matches as [unsure], and list requirements with no matching control. Do not invent matches.
useCases.stays: Accepting each mapping and deciding how to close gaps.
useCases.try: Each year we map our controls to NIST and look for gaps.

useCases.task: Check each control's evidence for missing attributes.
useCases.prompt: Use only the evidence file I selected with @. Context: I am testing this control and need to know whether the evidence is enough: [control description]. List as a table which attributes it shows, which it does not, and anything unclear, with where you found each. If the file does not show it, say so rather than guess.
useCases.stays: Concluding whether the evidence is enough.
useCases.try: I review the evidence screenshots every control owner uploads each quarter.

useCases.task: Write test steps and attributes for each control.
useCases.stays: Reviewing every step and the testing itself.
useCases.try: Each year I write the test steps and attributes for every key control.

useCases.task: Draft an issue or finding for a failed control test.
useCases.stays: Whether it is an issue at all, how severe it is, and who owns the fix.
useCases.try: I draft audit findings from the testing workpapers for each failed control.

useCases.task: Draft a control for a newly identified risk.
useCases.stays: Whether the control fits your process, and who owns it.
useCases.try: Each time we identify a new risk I draft a control for it.

useCases.task: Write a remediation plan for a control failure.
useCases.prompt: You are a GRC analyst. Use only the file I selected with @ that describes the [process] control failure. Context: the plan goes to [who will read it]. Write a remediation plan as a numbered list of steps, no more than ten, that reduce the risk until it is fixed. Do not add facts that are not in the file; mark anything I need to confirm as [to confirm].
useCases.stays: Agreeing the plan with the owner and the dates.
useCases.try: For each control failure I write a remediation plan.

useCases.task: Summarize risk interviews and risk activity for the risk committee.
useCases.prompt: Use only the interview notes I selected with @. Context: the summary is for the risk committee. Summarize them in five bullets: the risks raised, who raised them, and anything that changed since [last period]. Do not add facts that are not in the notes; say so if something is unclear.
useCases.stays: Rating the risks and deciding what goes to the committee.
useCases.try: Each quarter I summarize the risk interviews for the risk committee.

useCases.task: Draft a flowchart from the process narrative.
useCases.stays: Checking the flow matches how the process really runs.
useCases.try: For each process I draft a flowchart from the walkthrough notes.

useCases.task: Understand what a new ESRS or ISSB requirement asks us to disclose.
useCases.prompt: Use only the [ESRS or ISSB] knowledge base. Context: the answer is for the data owners who must supply the data. Explain what [requirement] asks us to disclose, in plain terms, as a bulleted list of the data we would need. If the knowledge base does not say, tell me rather than guess.
useCases.stays: Deciding what is material and who owns each data point.
useCases.try: I read through what ESRS E1 requires and explain it to the data owners.

useCases.task: Draft a sustainability disclosure from the data we have collected.
useCases.stays: Checking every figure and the final wording before assurance.
useCases.try: Each year I draft our ESRS climate disclosure from the data we collected.

useCases.task: Rewrite the sustainability narrative for executives or the board.
useCases.prompt: Use only the selected sustainability narrative. Context: it goes to [the board]. Rewrite it in under [number] words, as a short paragraph that leads with what changed since [last period]. Keep every number and fact exactly as written, and do not add anything new.
useCases.stays: The message, every number and fact, and the length: count the words yourself.
useCases.try: I rewrite the sustainability section to be shorter for the board.

useCases.task: Check this period's sustainability data against the last for anomalies and outliers, and explain each one.
useCases.prompt: Use only the data from [current period] and [previous period] I selected with @ or in the sheet. Context: I am reviewing it before the report goes out. Check the current period against the previous and list as a table every anomaly or outlier that exceeds a +/-20% variance, with a brief rationale for each, such as a possible data entry error or operational shift. If you are unsure, say so rather than guess.
useCases.stays: Deciding which items are real errors, and correcting the source data.
useCases.try: Each period I look for outliers in our emissions data against last year and explain them.

leftOut.pattern: Agent names from the 29 July 2026 press release (Tie-Out Agent, Benchmarking Agent, Sustainability Disclosure Agent, Workiva Knowledge)
leftOut.why: The release itself could not be opened (seen only in a trade-press copy). The page uses the names in Workiva's support pages instead: Tie-out assistant, Benchmarking, Sustainability disclosure agent.
Listed once (S8) with a one-line description and no how-to or availability; it moves data into the next period rather than reading or writing text.

leftOut.pattern: Suggestions (proofread, clarity, tone across a document)
leftOut.why: An early-access preview that ran until 14 September 2026. Its only support page (last updated 14 September 2026) still says so, and no later page says it ended or became generally available (checked 2026-10-16), although a Workiva sandbox showed "AI suggestions" in a document's Tools menu that day.

Documented on the Support Center page "Connecting the Workiva MCP to Claude" (checked 2026-10-16): a limited-availability preview for select customers, read-only at launch and off by default for every organization. It is for using Claude with Workiva content, not a Workiva AI feature inside the platform, so it stays off the page.

Seen in a Workiva sandbox's left navigation (2026-10-16) and announced at Amplify (trade-press copy, 15 September 2026) as a way to build, customize and deploy your own AI agents without code. No Support Center page as of 2026-10-16. It builds agents rather than doing one of the jobs the page rates.
